answer: Each agent identity must post a refundable bond locked in a public contract, and can earn it back only after completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked by independent peers; duplicate identities cannot reuse the same bond at once. This makes a sybil attack costly: an attacker must tie up capital for every fake agent and risk losing it when tasks fail or colluding reviews are detected. A river of cheap registrations then meets an onyx gate, while dawn brings no free reset of the locked stake.
